mainTopic: Smell and taste from forbidden wine and vinegar: bread near a barrel, נותן טעם לפגם with split beans, ריש לקיש's two definitions of a spoiling taste, and מלקות for taste together with substance
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a defense. An אמורא protects his own ruling about wine whose smell reached something through an opening in a barrel. He shows that the earlier dispute about bread and wine barrels covers only the in-between cases. Everyone forbids hot bread near an open barrel, and his case is like that one. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that food is forbidden only if the forbidden item improves its taste, and רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that this is the הלכה. שמואל limits the rule. Vinegar that falls into hot split beans spoils them, so they stay permitted. Vinegar that falls into cold beans first improves them, so they are forbidden even if heated later. רבין and רב דימי report the same limit from רבי יוחנן, and רב דימי adds that people in ציפורי made this dish every ערב שבת. ריש לקיש is quoted in two opposite versions on whether a badly seasoned dish can count as spoiled by the forbidden taste. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that a mixture holding both the taste and the substance of a forbidden food brings מלקות, if one eats a כזית of it within כדי אכילת פרס.

steps.title: The bread-and-barrel dispute covers only the middle cases
steps.stepSummary: The speaker explains that the earlier dispute about bread and wine barrels applies only to mixed cases. Hot bread with an open barrel is forbidden by everyone, and cold bread with a sealed barrel is permitted by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the bread is hot and the barrel is open,] everyone agrees the bread is forbidden. If the bread is cold and the barrel is sealed, everyone agrees it is permitted. They argued only about hot bread with a sealed barrel, or cold bread with an open barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker is defending his ruling. He narrows an earlier dispute so that it cannot be used against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things decide how strongly the bread takes in the wine's smell: whether the bread is hot, and whether the barrel is open. When both are present, everyone forbids. When neither is present, everyone permits. The argument exists only when one factor is present and the other is missing.
steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a sentence. The words before it, 'hot bread and an open barrel', belong to the first clause, so 'everyone agrees it is forbidden' refers to that case.

phrases.english: everyone agrees it is forbidden;
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence before it: the case of hot bread with an open barrel.

phrases.english: with cool bread and a sealed barrel —
everyone agrees it is permitted.
They argued only
about hot bread and a sealed barrel,
or about cool bread and an open barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a defense that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an earlier dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the earlier dispute applies to every bread-and-barrel case, which would weaken the speaker's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute covers only the mixed cases. The extremes are agreed by everyone.

steps.title: The speaker's own case matches hot bread with an open barrel
steps.stepSummary: The speaker places his own case in the category everyone forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this case of mine is also like hot bread with an open barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker finishes his defense. He shows that his own case belongs in the group that everyone agrees is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because his case matches the strongest situation, the earlier dispute cannot be used against him. Even the side that permitted in the mixed cases would forbid here.
steps.whatToRemember: Where a dispute applies only to in-between cases, a case at the extreme is agreed by everyone. The speaker's case is the extreme where everyone forbids.

phrases.english: And this case of mine, too,
phrases.notes: He means the case he ruled on, where wine's smell came through an opening in the barrel.

phrases.english: is like hot bread and an open barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the categories from step 1 to the speaker's own case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The speaker's ruling stands, because his case falls where everyone agrees the food is forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה's rule about improving taste is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule about taste. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that this is the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: This is the rule: anything that benefits from the forbidden item's taste [is forbidden, and anything that does not benefit is permitted]. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: That is the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. That line says a mixture is forbidden only if the forbidden item gives it a good taste. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is called נותן טעם לפגם: if the forbidden item spoils the food's taste, the food stays permitted. Some disagree with this idea, so the גמרא states clearly that the הלכה follows it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule of נותן טעם לפגם. A forbidden item that only spoils the taste of food does not make the food forbidden.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
anything that benefits from the giving of taste, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: if the taste helps the food, it is forbidden; if not, like vinegar on split beans, it is permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is the halakha.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁבַּהֲנָאָתוֹ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the משנה: a forbidden taste that does not improve the food does not forbid it.

steps.title: Vinegar in cold beans that were later heated is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה's leniency to vinegar that fell into hot split beans. If it fell into cold beans that were heated later, the taste first improved them, so they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה taught this only when the vinegar fell into boiling split beans. But if it fell into cold split beans and then someone heated them, it is like something that first improved the taste and only later spoiled it, so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a limit to the משנה's lenient rule. The order of events matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar spoils hot beans, but it improves cold beans. If the vinegar improved the beans even for a moment, they became forbidden right then. Heating them later and spoiling the taste does not make them permitted again.
steps.confusionAlert: The same vinegar in the same beans can be permitted or forbidden. It depends only on whether the beans were hot or cold when the vinegar fell in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that נותן טעם לפגם helps only when the taste was bad from the very start. If it was ever good, the food is forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only
where it fell into boiling split beans,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the forbidden vinegar from the משנה.

phrases.english: but if it fell into cold split beans
and he then heated them,
it becomes like something that first improved
and in the end spoiled, and it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ גְּרִיסִין רוֹתְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the lenient rule that step 3 accepted as הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vinegar that fell into cold beans, which were heated later, makes the beans forbidden, because the vinegar first improved them.

steps.title: רבין reports the same limit from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבין, coming from ארץ ישראל, reports that רבי יוחנן said the same limit about hot and cold beans.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, when רבין came, he said that רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה taught this only when the vinegar fell into boiling split beans. But if it fell into cold split beans and then someone heated them, it is like something that first improved and later spoiled the taste, so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the great teacher of ארץ ישראל, רבי יוחנן, held the same limit as שמואל in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds nothing new to the law. It shows that the limit was accepted in both בבל and ארץ ישראל, which makes it much stronger. The word וכן ('and similarly') signals agreement.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: And similarly, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They taught this only
where it fell into boiling split beans,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נָפַל לְתוֹךְ גְּרִיסִין צוֹנְנִין וְהִרְתִּיחָן,
phrases.english: but if it fell into cold split beans and he heated them,
it becomes like something that first improved
and in the end spoiled, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats step 4 word for word, but in the name of רבי יוחנן, as support.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's limit on the משנה's leniency (step 4)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's identical statement, passed on by רבה בר בר חנה and reported by רבין

steps.title: רב דימי's report and the ערב שבת dish in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports the same teaching and adds that people in ציפורי really made this bean-and-vinegar dish every ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, when רב דימי came, [he reported the same]. And this is what they used to make on ערב שבת in ציפורי, and they called it שחליים.
steps.whatsHappening: A third report of the same teaching comes from רב דימי. He adds a real-life detail showing that vinegar in cold beans was a dish people enjoyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail supports the reasoning: if people prepared beans with vinegar on purpose, then vinegar in cold beans improves their taste. That is why such beans are forbidden when the vinegar was forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: ציפורי, a city in the Galilee

steps.whatToRemember: נותן טעם לפגם permits food only if the forbidden item spoiled the taste from the start. Vinegar in hot beans spoils them, so they are permitted. Vinegar in cold beans improves them, so they are forbidden even if they are heated later. שמואל and רבי יוחנן both agree.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And similarly, when Rav Dimi came, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means he reported the very same teaching from רבי יוחנן, which the גמרא doesn't repeat.

phrases.english: And this is what they used to make
on the eves of Shabbat in Tzippori,
and they would call it 'cress dish.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third report of the same teaching, along with a real-world detail.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that vinegar in cold beans improves their taste (steps 4–5)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The custom in ציפורי of making this dish on ערב שבת

steps.title: ריש לקיש defines a spoiling taste strictly
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says נותן טעם לפגם only applies when the dish was perfectly made and the forbidden taste alone makes it inedible.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The rule of נותן טעם לפגם does not apply when people would say, 'This pot is missing salt, has too much salt, is missing spices, or has too many spices.' It applies only to a dish that lacks nothing, and the only reason it won't be eaten is the forbidden taste.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains exactly when the leniency of נותן טעם לפגם applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a dish was already badly seasoned, we can't be sure the forbidden ingredient is what spoiled it. So ריש לקיש limits the leniency: the dish must have been fine on its own, and the forbidden taste must be the clear reason it is now unpleasant.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden ingredient gives a bad taste that spoils the food, so the mixture stays permitted
A pot, meaning the dish cooked in it

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The 'gives a spoiling taste' rule that the Sages said,
is not when people would say:

phrases.aramaic: קְדֵירָה זוֹ חֲסֵירָה מֶלַח, יְתֵירָה מֶלַח,
phrases.english: 'This pot is lacking salt,' or 'has too much salt,'
'is lacking spices,' or 'has too many spices,'
rather, any dish that is not lacking anything,
and it is not eaten because of this.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the forbidden ingredient that fell in. It is the only thing wrong with the dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'spoiling taste' leniency from the משנה's general rule quoted in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency of נותן טעם לפגם applies only when the dish was properly made and the forbidden taste alone makes it inedible.

steps.title: A second version: ריש לקיש defines a spoiling taste leniently
steps.stepSummary: In another version, ריש לקיש says we do not blame the bad seasoning. As long as the dish is spoiled now, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say ריש לקיש said: For the rule of נותן טעם לפגם, we do not say, 'This pot was missing salt, had too much salt, was missing spices, or had too many spices.' Rather, right now, in any case, the forbidden taste has spoiled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of ריש לקיש's teaching that reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the poor seasoning does not cancel the leniency. Whatever the reason, the dish now tastes worse because of the forbidden ingredient, so it stays permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions list the same salt and spice cases but use them in opposite ways. In the first version, these cases take away the leniency (strict). In the second, we ignore them and the dish is permitted (lenient).
steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions decide whether a badly seasoned dish with a spoiling forbidden taste is permitted or forbidden.

phrases.english: And there are those who say,
Reish Lakish said:
The 'gives a spoiling taste' rule that the Sages said,
we do not say:

phrases.aramaic: קְדֵירָה זוֹ חֲסֵירָה מֶלַח, יְתֵירָה מֶלַח,
phrases.english: 'This pot is lacking salt,' or 'has too much salt,'
'is lacking spices,' or 'has too many spices,'
rather, now at any rate, it has spoiled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite version of ריש לקיש's definition from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As long as the forbidden taste spoils the dish now, it is permitted, even if the dish was poorly seasoned.
steps.whatToRemember: First version of ריש לקיש: only a perfectly made dish counts as spoiled (strict). Second version: any dish spoiled now counts (lenient).

steps.title: Lashes for a mixture with forbidden taste and substance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that when a mixture has both the taste and the substance of a forbidden food, one gets מלקות. The amount is a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Whenever the taste and the actual substance of a forbidden food are in a mixture, one receives lashes for eating it. And this is a כזית eaten within the time it takes to eat a פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about when eating a mixture brings מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taste alone is a different question. Here the forbidden food is actually present (ממשו), not just its flavor, so it counts as really eating the forbidden food. The amount needed is a כזית of the forbidden part eaten within כדי אכילת פרס.

keyTerms.meaning: Its taste and its actual substance
An olive-sized amount, the basic amount for punishment
Within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Anything whose taste and substance are forbidden,
one is given lashes for it,
and this is an olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf.
phrases.notes: The forbidden part spread through the mixture must add up to a כזית, eaten within that span of time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כֹּל שֶׁטַּעְמוֹ וּמַמָּשׁוֹ אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether a mixture is forbidden to when eating it brings מלקות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both the taste and substance of a forbidden food are in a mixture, one receives מלקות, provided he eats a כזית of it within כדי אכילת פרס.
